Thought: I need to determine which isotopic pair would exhibit the largest isotope effect. The isotope effect refers to the difference in reaction rates or equilibrium constants when an atom in a molecule is replaced by one of its isotopes. The magnitude of the isotope effect is generally related to the relative mass difference between the isotopes.

Let me analyze each option:

A. Carbon-12 and carbon-13: The mass difference is 1 amu (atomic mass unit), and the relative mass difference is 1/12 ≈ 8.3%.

B. Carbon-12 and carbon-14: The mass difference is 2 amu, and the relative mass difference is 2/12 ≈ 16.7%.

C. Hydrogen and deuterium: Hydrogen has a mass of 1 amu, and deuterium has a mass of 2 amu. The mass difference is 1 amu, and the relative mass difference is 1/1 = 100%.

D. Nitrogen-14 and nitrogen-15: The mass difference is 1 amu, and the relative mass difference is 1/14 ≈ 7.1%.

The isotope effect is largest when the relative mass difference is largest. Among these options, hydrogen and deuterium have the largest relative mass difference (100%), so they would exhibit the largest isotope effect.
